earlier_scan.source_named: Only classificatory refs (Bennett 1983, Boyd 1989, Kastenholz 2017) on Glottolog; no description of Koke located online.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Raimund Kastenholz, Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer & Florian Lionnet. 2020. The Bua group noun class system: looking for a historical interpretation. Language in Africa 1(3): 181-215. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-181-215 (published version of the 2019 Mainz noun-class handout in our bibliography)
sources.note: Nothing: a full-text search of the extracted text output for tone/tonal/tones/stress/accent/prosod returns zero hits; Koke occurs only in Table 1 and the p.184 dialect remark.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2020. Personal pronouns in Bua languages. Language in Africa 1(3): 292-335. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-292-335 (published version of the 2019 Mainz handout that is in our bibliography)
sources.note: Nothing on Koke. p.325 fn.15: 'the author of Bolgo(3) worked with people from Bolgo Dugag and from Koke (Tikka 2019: 11)'; p.327: 'For the time being nothing can be said concerning Zan Gula, Bon Gula, and Bolgo, in which the tonal identity of personals is still missing.' The only 'stress' token (p.300, Tun) concerns vowel variants of object vs possessive pronouns 'and a difference of resulting syllable stress' — Tun, not Koke, and not a word-stress rule.

sources.citation: Lionnet, Florian. 2020. Kulaale (Chad) – Language Snapshot. Language Documentation and Description 17: 126-133. doi:10.25894/ldd103
sources.note: p.127: Inland Bua split 'between Bolgo/Koke and Gula'; p.130 documentation overview (Kastenholz 2017 Bolgo Kubar; Tikka 2019 Bolgo Dugag; other Bua languages unpublished). Nothing on Koke phonology; Kulaale tone two heights. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2019. The personal pronouns of the Bua languages: a comparative overview (Adamawa Conference 2019, Mainz, handout); and Boyeldieu, Kastenholz, Kleinewillinghöfer & Lionnet. 2019. The evolution of the Bua group noun class system (same conference)
sources.note: No Koke data and no stress/accent content (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Tikka, Katie Ann. 2019. Phonology and morphology of Bolgo. MA thesis, University of North Dakota, Grand Forks. xiii+156 pp. (UND Theses and Dissertations 2869;https://commons.und.edu/theses/2869)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Closest description to Koke (author worked with Koke speakers from Daguéla). p.1: thesis 'also contain[s] details concerning the Bolgo Kubar dialect and the Koke language, which is closely related to Bolgo'; p.2: Koke 'is sometimes grouped in as if it were a third dialect of Bolgo (Sauer 2008: 4)', 68% / 60% lexical similarity with Bolgo Dugag / Kubar (Faris & Meundeung 1993b), 90.1% per Boyeldieu et al. Koke remarks are segmental only (more word-medial voiceless stops, no retroflex flap [ɽ], no word-final stops, plural -ti). §2.4 Tone pp.44-45 (Bolgo Dugag): three level tones H/M/L, TBU = sy…

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Raimund Kastenholz, Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer & Florian Lionnet. 2018. The Bua Group languages (Chad, Adamawa 13): A comparative perspective. In Raija Kramer & Roland Kießling (eds), Current approaches to Adamawa and Gur languages (AuÜ Supplements 34), 53-126. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. [HAL author version halshs-03096908, 58 pp., and published version 75 pp. from Lionnet's site]
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent/'accent' = 0 hits). Koke: inventory p.56 (published) = HAL p.2 (600 speakers; Daguéla, Chobo); p.58-59 Koke known only from Nachtigal's wordlist in Lukas 1937 and the Faris & Meundeung 1993 SIL wordlist (plus an unpublished Pairault list); fn.13 p.61: 'Koke is argued here to be part of a dialectally structured Bolgo Complex'; p.63: 'As for several other features, the situation of Koke is not known.' §4.4 Tones p.71: 'Ɓa, Lua, Tun, and Bolgo have tone systems with three contrastive heights (Low, Mid, and High)'; §5.5 p.…

sources.citation: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2017. La langue bolgo du Guéra (Tchad): Notes de recherche et matériel lexical. (Arbeitspapiere des Instituts für Ethnologie und Afrikastudien der JGU Mainz 172.) 48 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Bolgo Kubar sketch. pp.3-4: 'je préfère parler d'un continuum bolgo, dont le koke, très probablement, ferait partie'; Koke data used = Lukas 1937 and Faris/Meundeung 1993b only. §2.1.3 Ton p.8: Bolgo has 'un sytème tonal de trois niveaux distinctifs, haut (H), moyen (M) et bas (B)'. No accent/stress; no Koke phonology.

sources.citation: Brenzinger, Matthias (ed.). 2007. Language Diversity Endangered. (Trends in Linguistics. Studies and Monographs 181.) Berlin / New York: Mouton de Gruyter. xvii+454 pp. [copies we hold is the complete volume; African chapters read: ch. 6 Brenzinger 'Language Endangerment in Northern Africa' 123–139; ch. 7 Blench 'Endangered Languages in West Africa' 140–162; ch. 8 Connell 'Endangered Languages in Central Africa' 163–178; ch. 9 Brenzinger 'Language Endangerment in Southern and Eastern Africa' 179–204]
sources.note: Nothing on stress/tone: table row only — 'Majority bilingual in Shuwa Arabic or Fania'.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 1988. Présentation sommaire du groupe Boua (Tchad) (Adamawa 13 de J.H. Greenberg). In Daniel Barreteau & Henry Tourneux (eds), Le milieu et les hommes: recherches comparatives et historiques dans le bassin du lac Tchad. Actes du 2ème colloque Méga-Tchad, ORSTOM Bondy, 3-4 octobre 1985 (Colloques et séminaires), 275-286. Paris: ORSTOM. [also as Cahiers du LACITO 1: 19-29, 1986]
sources.note: p.276: Koke known from Nachtigal and 'les notes de A.F. zu Mecklenburg sur le koke' published by Lukas 1937. p.280-281 §2 'A défaut de matériaux suffisemment précis pour l'ensemble du groupe, la comparaison des seuls 4 parlers (kulaal, tun, lua et 'ba)..'; §2.1: 'Tun, lua et 'ba connaissent des systèmes tonals à 3 registres (avec différentes modulations possibles) dont l'unité fonctionnelle serait plutôt représentée par le schème tonal du "mot" dans son ensemble. C. Pairault propose pour le kulaal une analyse en 2 hauteurs pertinentes'. Nothing on Koke tone or on stress/accent in any Bua lang…

sources.citation: de Rendinger, Général. 1949. Contribution à l'étude des langues nègres du Centre Africain. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 19(2): 143-194.
sources.note: Grammar notes and wordlists of 'Bolgo Werel' (Daguéla), which Tikka 2019: 10-11 identifies as Koke; oldest quasi-grammatical data on Koke, may carry accent marks or a remark on accent.

sources.citation: Homburger, L. 1938. [Compte rendu de] Lukas (J.). Zentralsudanische Studien. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 8(2): 213-214.
sources.note: no phonology content; bibliographic pointer confirming what the Lukas 1937 Koke section contains (wordlists/notes), no mention of tone or accent notation.

sources.citation: Sauer, Silke. 2008. Une esquisse phonologique de la langue bolgo du Guéra. Ms. N'Djaména: SIL Tchad.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Phonological sketch of Bolgo that treats Koke as a third dialect and contains Koke details (Tikka 2019: 2, 11); the one phonology document with Koke data, may carry a tone/prosody statement.

sources.citation: Faris, David & Marba Meundeung. 1993. Etude sociolinguistique de la langue koke du Guéra. N'Djaména: SIL Tchad. (survey report with c. 160-word list; cited as 1993b by Kastenholz 2017/Tikka 2019 and 1993d by Boyeldieu et al. 2018)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only document devoted to Koke; a sociolinguistic survey with a wordlist (tone not transcribed per Lionnet 2020: 130 for the sister Fanya report), so unlikely to state stress, but it is the sole Koke-specific primary record.

sources.citation: Hersé, P.L. 1947. Observations sur les margayes de Melfi. Bulletin de l'Institut d'Etudes Centrafricaines (Brazzaville) II(1): 1-97.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Ethnographic report on the Melfi 'margayes' incl. the Koke of Daguéla (Ourel); cited for Koke names and population by Boyeldieu et al. 2018 and Tucker & Bryan 1956; low chance of a stress statement.

sources.citation: Lukas, Johannes. 1937. Zentralsudanische Studien: Wörterverzeichnisse der Deutschen Zentral-Afrika-Expedition 1910/11, nachgelassene Aufnahmen von Gustav Nachtigal und eigene Sammlungen. Hamburg: Friederichsen, de Gruyter. pp. 52-70 (Bua-Gruppe: Bua, Nielim, Koke).

sources.note: Nachtigal's c. 1880 Koke wordlist, the basis of Greenberg's Adamawa-13; Glottolog's only overview ref for Koke. Wordlist only; stress remark unlikely but unchecked.

sources.citation: Pairault, Claude. [1960s]. Unpublished Koke wordlist (manuscript field file, cited as '\kok_P koke: Pairault man.' in Boyeldieu et al. 2018 Table 12, and as 'Pairault, Claude.. Bolgo, Koke' under unpublished documentation, p. 126).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only tone-marked (Pairault marked tone in his Kulaal work) lexical data on Koke, held by Boyeldieu/LLACAN; would show whether Koke is tonal like Bolgo.
